packs.title: Gardens and New Angles
packs.promise: Read another Kraków through southern architecture, western green spaces and Nowa Huta.

q.s: Build an original composition around an empty space.
st: From a comfortable stopped public position, find the modern rust-coloured frame, an older gabled building and a visible gap between them.
Make an original small composition on paper or your device using one broad dark mark for the frame and one small mark for the old building. Leave a deliberate blank gap.
Give your composition a short caption of your own about what the empty space does. Save the marks or describe their arrangement in words.

q.s: Find three distances in one open view.
st: From one stopped perimeter position, find a near detail, a middle-distance patch and a far edge of the meadow view.
Give each layer one short word or original mark. Change the mark’s size to show how near or far it feels; no measured distance is needed.
Save your three layers and choose which gives the open meadow its sense of space.

q.s: Make an original note from a pond’s edge.
st: Choose three ingredients from one stopped view: a bank line, an open patch of water and a built shape or tree cluster on the opposite side.
Make an original three-line message or three-mark composition. Let one line follow the bank, leave one open gap for water, and place the last mark across it.
Save your composition with one short sentence about where it sends your eye. A written arrangement and drawing earn equal credit.

packs.title: Rooflines and River Notes
packs.promise: Find a small story in Kraków’s rooflines, courtyard shapes and riverside textures.

q.s: Collect three shapes on the Cloth Hall’s long facade.
st: Choose an open square-side view of the Cloth Hall, leaving room beside entrances and outdoor tables.
Find three shapes at different heights: an arcade opening, a rectangular window and a curl or point along the decorative upper edge.
Give each shape a short name of your own. Arrange the names from lowest to highest.
Choose which shape would make the best first letter in an imaginary alphabet and explain your choice.

q.s: Give a Main Market Square detail two different beginnings.
st: Find a comfortable public stopping place with a view of a townhouse window and the coloured facade around it.
Choose one visible detail, such as a curved frame, a pale ledge or a patch of shadow.
Write two original opening sentences about that same detail. Let one feel lively and the other feel unhurried.
Read them silently and keep the opening you prefer, along with the detail that started both.

q.t: A Small Story under a Roof
q.s: Let a Wawel tower’s outline start a tiny story.
st: Find a comfortable open public viewpoint below Wawel Hill where the round brick Sandomierska Tower and its red tiled roof are visible.
Choose a small pale-framed window and a sloping line on the roof above it.
Write a three-sentence original story that begins with the window, changes direction at the roofline and ends in the sky.
Read it silently and save the story with the two shapes that guided it.
